scope: All 13 completed stills manually viewed: 8 authored raster compositions and 5 ray-traced images. Composition/material/lighting review only; no continuous-motion, native-FPS or survey-accuracy claim. Root independently accepted the three principal RT day/sunset/night stills.
findings: All eight compositions show the intended skyline from a distinct shore/offshore angle, without blocking camera geometry.
Adler day/sunset/night keep Willis Tower and the northern silhouette readable; vertical fields of view were narrowed before this only gallery run.
The matched view-2 sunset has an amber/rose sky and warm RT water reflections; day and night at exactly the same camera differ coherently.
North Avenue view emphasizes Hancock; Burnham harbor and elevated offshore views show the lakefront context.
No duplicate skyline geometry or separate world introduced.
limitations: Existing daylight aerial haze reduces distant facade contrast.
Night water is restrained/dark; RT reflections retain some finite-sample grain.
Distant skyline facades and some heights remain procedural interpretations, rather than a photogrammetric replica.
Raster reflections show the analytic atmosphere/sun rather than local building reflections and occlusion; sunset sun glare is therefore stronger than in RT.
Sunset is a smooth analytic gradient without the reference photograph cloud shapes, not an ephemeris or measured atmosphere.
